summary.text: Sydney Gruters is the Republican nominee for the open 16th District seat, endorsed by President Trump. She spent years on congressional staffs and held a federal agriculture post in the first Trump administration before working at the New College Foundation in Sarasota. This is her first run for office; her campaign materials emphasize lowering costs, border security and election security.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, she is a native Floridian and a working mother of three.
Worked for more than a decade in Washington, D.C., and Manatee County for Rep. Vern Buchanan, whose seat she is now seeking, according to her campaign website.
According to her campaign website, was appointed by President Trump in 2017 as State Director for Florida and the U.S. Virgin Islands at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Rural Development.
Served as district director for Rep. Greg Steube after his 2018 election, according to her campaign website.
Most recently served as vice president of advancement and executive director of the New College Foundation, per her campaign website and WGCU.
Is married to Joe Gruters, a Florida state senator and chairman of the Republican National Committee, according to her campaign website and WGCU.
WGCU reports this is her first bid for elected office. She won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 63.6% of the vote over Eddie Speir and Ed Pope.

sources.title: Three very different candidates vying for Congress in Florida District 16
